```js
for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
  setTimeout(async () => {
    console.log('timeout', i);
    await Promise.resolve();
    console.log('after await', i);
  }, 0);
}
console.log('sync done');
```
**Answer:**
```
sync done
timeout 0
after await 0
timeout 1
after await 1
timeout 2
after await 2
```
**Why:** All synchronous code runs first (`'sync done'`). Then each `setTimeout` macrotask runs one at a time — but crucially, ALL microtasks generated by one macrotask (including the `await Promise.resolve()` resumption) fully drain **before the next macrotask begins**. So each timeout's `'timeout N'` and `'after await N'` pair completes together before the next timeout callback starts, rather than all three `'timeout'` logs happening first.
